title: Influence of a bribed coordinate
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and choose a sign $b$. If $i$ belongs to $J$, then the influence of the function obtained by setting every coordinate in $J$ to $b$ before applying $f$ is zero in coordinate $i$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
